approach: A `cargo` symlink to the athena binary sits in a per-job wrapper directory that is first on the producer's PATH. `main` sees argv[0] is `cargo`, reads the job's slot settings from env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT`, finds the real cargo further down PATH and, for build, check, clippy, test, doc and run, calls `slot_exec::run`, the same function behind the hidden `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` subcommand. `run` takes a producer-class slot from the real `SlotQueue`, appends one JSON line (subcommand, queued_s, slots held) to a per-job log and runs the command as a plain child in the wrapper's own process group, so group kills still reach the build tree. The child's env carries `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1`, so a nested cargo passes through. A wait past the limit prints `no build slot free for <N> s; try again` and exits 75. The slot is a file lock, so the OS frees it on any exit. The producer's wait limit is `min(build_wait_s, bash_default_timeout_ms/1000 − 60)`; the interaction with ageing is stated, tested as a pure property and raised as a User question (round-4 finding 7). In the hook, a producer-role policy denies a slotted cargo unless the wrapper dir (env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_BIN`) holds a `cargo` file and the first `cargo` on the hook's PATH is that one; a missing variable denies. `invoke_and_record` reads and removes the wrapper log into an optional `Invocation.build_slots`, where `slotted_seen` is the honest count of slotted cargo commands in `commands_run` (no fake-driver flag; status skips the note when `driver.name == "fake"`). The 'build wait' line adds producer waits, the peak slots held and the unslotted note. `reading.rs::agent_spec` installs the wrapper under the same `side == Side::Produce` test env.rs uses. Producer commands only; no unsafe code; no non-Rust file.

decisions.choice: The wrapper is a symlink named `cargo` to the athena binary, dispatched on argv[0] in `main` beside the existing `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` dispatch (main.rs ~546-553). A hidden clap variant `build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` calls the same `slot_exec::run`.
decisions.reason: No shell script is needed (Rust-only default). `-- <cmd>` is the form the design names, and tests and the wrapper share one code path.

rejected.option: A `#!/bin/sh` wrapper script that execs `athena build-slot -- cargo "$@"`
rejected.why: It adds a non-Rust file and needs its own recursion guard.

rejected.option: Having the hook rewrite the command to `athena build-slot -- cargo ...`
rejected.why: It needs new hook output and changes what commands_run holds. The design says a PATH wrapper.

decisions.choice: Re-entrancy: `run` sets `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1` in the child's env; `cargo_wrapper` and `build-slot` check it first and, if set, run with no slot and no log line. Names are constants in athena-agent `lib.rs`. Every slot_exec test builds its child Command through one helper `scrubbed()` (env_clear, explicit PATH, only the slot variables the test needs). `real_cargo` takes PATH and its own path as arguments.
decisions.reason: The wrapper dir stays first on PATH for everything the wrapped command starts. Repo tests start `cargo` by name (slots.rs:824, run/tests.rs:2659, disk.rs:824, xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:121); with max_check_slots = 1 (config.rs:165) a nested cargo would wait for a second slot and time out. The marker would also make these tests pass through unslotted when a later producer runs `cargo test` through its own wrapper, so tests must not inherit it (crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:289-291 does the same for ATHENA_NESTED). The policy denies `NAME=value` prefixes (policy.rs:546-553), so a producer cannot set the marker.

rejected.option: Remove the wrapper dir from the child's PATH
rejected.why: String-edits PATH and stops later nested calls from being checked.

rejected.option: Let tests inherit the process env
rejected.why: CI passes (no wrapper) while every later producer's run of these tests would fail.

decisions.choice: The child is a plain `Command::spawn` in the wrapper's own process group: no `procs::isolate`, no signal handler. Exit code is the child's, or 128+signal.
decisions.reason: procs.rs:88-92 `isolate` moves the child to a new group, so group kills (Registry::stop_all, kill_group on deadline) would miss rustc and test binaries. `unsafe_code = deny` rules out a new signal handler outside procs.rs.

rejected.option: procs::isolate
rejected.why: Takes the build tree out of the agent's group.

rejected.option: A pub parent-death helper in procs.rs
rejected.why: procs.rs is not a deliverable; the gap (wrapper alone SIGKILLed) is stated in the Built note.

decisions.choice: The wrapper reads its queue from `{job_dir}/build-slot.json` (slots dir, slots, wait_s, promote_s), named by env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT`; log path in `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG`; wrapper dir in `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_BIN`. `SlotSettings::producer(dir, &pipeline, bash_default_timeout_ms)` caps wait_s at `bash_default_timeout_ms/1000 − 60` (min 1) and keeps `promote_s = build_age_promote_s` from the pipeline unchanged.
decisions.reason: config.rs:166 gives 1800 s, athena.toml:64-65 sets Bash timeouts of 600 s/1200 s, env.rs:81-88 passes them to the agent. A wrapper that waits 1800 s is killed first by the Bash tool and the producer never sees the message. The agent's ATHENA_STATE_DIR is the nested job state (env.rs:97-100), so the shared slots dir must be written down; EnvSpec is built in about ten places so it gets no new fields. promote_s is NOT changed per role: is_head (slots.rs:298-308) orders every ticket with the reader's own promote, so processes using different intervals would disagree on the head and every waiter could stall.

rejected.option: Write build_wait_s unchanged
rejected.why: The shipped config could not show the behavior asked for.

rejected.option: Give the producer its own smaller promote_s
rejected.why: Readers with different intervals disagree on which ticket is head (slots.rs:298-308); waiters could stall to timeout.

rejected.option: New fields on EnvSpec
rejected.why: Forces edits at every EnvSpec literal.

decisions.choice: Cap versus ageing (round-4 finding 7): state it, test it as a pure property, and ask. Add `SlotSettings::ages_into_check_class(&self) -> bool` (true when wait_s >= promote_s, the point where a Producer ticket ties a Check ticket under the is_head rule `effective = class − age/promote`, slots.rs:37-44, 298-308). A slots.rs test shows it is false for `producer(…, build_wait_s 1800, 600000)` under the shipped defaults (wait 540 < promote 600) and true for an uncapped 1800 s wait, so the test documents the loss instead of hiding it. The Risks and the Built note say: a retry makes a new ticket with a fresh queued_at (slots.rs:245-251), so retries never build up age; with max_check_slots = 1 and a steady stream of checks a producer can wait to exit 75 without promotion. A User question asks for `build_age_promote_s` below the cap in a governance job (athena.toml is out of scope).
decisions.reason: The design (agent-and-build-slots.md:155-156) says ageing exists so the producer class cannot starve behind checks. The Bash timeout cap makes a wait over the promote interval impossible with the shipped numbers. The fix lies in governance config or a larger Bash timeout, outside this job; the plan must not hide it.

rejected.option: Per-role promote_s in the producer's settings
rejected.why: Breaks head agreement between processes (see decision 4).

rejected.option: Raise the cap above the Bash timeout
rejected.why: The producer never sees the exit 75 message.

rejected.option: Warn at runtime in the wrapper
rejected.why: The wrapper has no output channel the producer reads besides its own stderr; the check is static and belongs in a test and the docs.

decisions.choice: Slotted subcommands are build, check, clippy, test, doc and run, defined once in athena-agent `lib.rs` (`takes_build_slot`, `cargo_subcommand`) and used by the policy, the wrapper and the seen-count. fmt, metadata and tree pass through.
decisions.reason: Design section 4 asks for every cargo command that compiles. The producer may run doc and run (athena.toml:74), so leaving them out lets a build happen outside a slot. The Built note states that `cargo run` and `cargo test` hold a slot for the whole program run.

rejected.option: Only build, test, clippy, check
rejected.why: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` would compile outside the limit.

rejected.option: For `run`, slot only a `cargo build` then exec the binary
rejected.why: Needs cargo argument parsing and two invocations; a later refinement.

decisions.choice: The wrapper rule is read from the environment, not a new `Policy` field. In policy.rs a private `enum BuildWrapper { NotRequired, Required { dir: Option<PathBuf>, path: Option<OsString> } }` is built by `BuildWrapper::from_env(role, lookup)`: Required for `Role::Producer`, NotRequired otherwise. `evaluate` keeps its signature and calls a new `evaluate_in(policy, tool, input, cwd, &BuildWrapper)`; `check_bash`, `check_segment`, `check_cargo` gain the argument. For Required and `takes_build_slot(sub)`, deny unless `dir` is Some, `<dir>/cargo` is a file, and the first PATH directory holding a file `cargo` is `dir` (canonicalized). The test helper `bash` uses NotRequired.
decisions.reason: Existing denials (`/usr/bin/cargo`, `./cargo`, `+nightly`, `--target-dir`) already exist; the new rule must catch a different cargo winning PATH. Reading env leaves `Policy` unchanged, removing literal edits in admission.rs, run/planning.rs, tests/refusal_corpus.rs and tests/live.rs (every Policy literal outside policy.rs and reading.rs is a Verifier policy: refusal_corpus.rs:1030/1191, admission.rs:688/818/903, planning.rs:219, live.rs:170). The hook inherits the agent's env (hooks.rs:52-78). A missing variable denies (fails closed).

rejected.option: A new `Policy.build_wrapper` field
rejected.why: Needs a value at ten literals in six non-deliverable files.

rejected.option: Only check that `<dir>/cargo` exists
rejected.why: Detects a missing install, not a cargo resolving elsewhere.

rejected.option: Skip the rule when the env variable is absent
rejected.why: The check would silently turn off; for a producer absence denies.

decisions.choice: Wrapper install and env share one condition (round-4 finding 9): in `reading.rs::agent_spec` the settings file and wrapper are written when `side == Side::Produce`, the same test env.rs uses to put the wrapper first on PATH and set the variables. `BuildWrapper::from_env` keys on `Role::Producer`; run/producer.rs:166 is the only caller that passes Side::Produce and it passes the Producer role. The reading.rs test asserts the pair: a Side::Produce spec has the wrapper `cargo` symlink, build-slot.json and the three variables, and a Side::Verify/Side::Read spec has none of them.
decisions.reason: Two different conditions could diverge: every slotted cargo would be denied, or a wrapper installed that nothing points to. Gating on `side` ties install to env; the test ties both to the policy's Producer role.

rejected.option: Gate the install on role == Role::Producer
rejected.why: Differs from the env.rs condition (Side::Produce).

rejected.option: A debug_assert tying role and side in agent_spec
rejected.why: Not run in release; the test is the mechanism.

decisions.choice: Keep `commands_run: Vec<String>`. Add one optional sibling `Invocation.build_slots: Option<BuildSlots>` with `BuildSlots { commands: Vec<CommandSlot>, slotted_seen: u32 }` and `CommandSlot { subcommand, queued_s, slots_held }`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
decisions.reason: commands_run is read as strings by display.rs:1656, status.rs:1707, verify.rs:366; changing its element type breaks them and old records. A fixed word and numbers need no redaction. One optional struct means each literal needs only `build_slots: None`.

rejected.option: Make commands_run elements a struct or untagged enum
rejected.why: Changes every reader and the old-record read path.

rejected.option: Two sibling fields
rejected.why: Two more literal entries per site for one idea.

decisions.choice: Bypass check with an honest record (round-4 finding 10): `invoke_and_record` calls a pure `build_slots_record(log_text: Option<&str>, commands_run: &[String])` with no driver flag. `slotted_seen = athena_agent::slotted_cargo_commands(commands_run)` (splits on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, newline; counts segments whose program is exactly `cargo` with a slotted subcommand). The record is None when there is no log and nothing seen. The unslotted note in status.rs is skipped when the invocation's `driver.name == "fake"` (the fake driver's name, athena-agent/src/fake.rs:82; reading.rs:408 uses the same test), because a fake driver runs no real PATH resolution and its tests list `cargo test` in commands_run (run/tests.rs:4805). The Built note names this as a test-driver exception in the status reader, not in the record.
decisions.reason: The record states what was seen; the reader decides whether a mismatch is meaningful. The wrapper's log is the ground truth of what went through; commands_run is the ground truth of what the producer ran.

rejected.option: A `fake: bool` argument that zeroes the count in the record builder
rejected.why: Production record code would branch on test drivers and store a dishonest zero.

rejected.option: A warning line in invoke_and_record
rejected.why: invocation.rs has no output sink and the record would show nothing afterwards.

rejected.option: Subtract policy_denials from seen
rejected.why: Denial.detail is free text and does not name the command; the note states the overcount.

decisions.choice: Exit 75 with the documented message is the whole timeout handling for producer commands; no hold marker is written. 'Held, not failed' is read as: the producer's job is not failed and no attempt is spent. The design (agent-and-build-slots.md:164-165) leaves the decision to the producer after exit 75. The gap with the request's 'held' is a User question and stated in the Built note and CHANGELOG. The 'not failed' half is shown by one invocation.rs test (decision 12) and by the argument that no code path turns a command's exit code into job state (the wrapper has no job-state access; its settings hold only the slots dir and limits).
decisions.reason: A run-level hold would reach into the step-3 files, which are out of scope.

rejected.option: A run-level test with a fake producer whose command exits 75
rejected.why: A command's exit code never reaches job state; the test would repeat the design text.

rejected.option: Writing a slot-wait hold marker from the wrapper
rejected.why: Needs job-state access and edits to out-of-scope step-3 files.

decisions.choice: The peak is carried per producer command as `slots_held`: `Slot::held()` counts locked slot files just after the slot is won. The status line prints the maximum, labelled 'when a producer command started' (a lower bound). Tests assert `overlap <= limit`, `held <= limit` and `max held >= forced overlap`, never exact equality. Overlap is forced by barriers and measured apart from the lock files; a control runs the same commands unwrapped and must read overlap above the limit.
decisions.reason: A count over N lock files is at most N by construction, so 'held <= limit' alone cannot fail. Equality is flaky (a holder may decrement before it drops its lock); a forced barrier makes `>=` deterministic.

rejected.option: Assert Slot::held() <= limit only
rejected.why: True by construction.

rejected.option: A peak counter file in the slots dir
rejected.why: Stale after SIGKILL; status reads records, not the slots dir.

decisions.choice: Demonstrating 'job not failed' (round-4 finding 8): an invocation.rs test runs `invoke_and_record` with the existing fake driver whose scripted result has `cargo test` in commands_run, with a wrapper log already written at the path in `spec.env[ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG]` that holds a line, and asserts the call returns Ok with the driver's outcome fields unchanged and `build_slots` filled. The criterion 3 demonstration says plainly that this shows the record path does not turn a recorded command into a failure, and that the exit-75-holds-nothing half is a design argument, not a run-level test.
decisions.reason: The criterion names the behavior; a cheap test covers what can be reached without step-3 files, and the rest is stated so the verifier does not expect a test.

rejected.option: A run/tests.rs run-level test
rejected.why: run/tests.rs is a step-3 file, out of scope.

decisions.choice: Out-of-list edits stay limited to the data path: reading.rs (`agent_spec` writes the settings and installs the wrapper), invocation.rs (builds the record), pr_check.rs, reconcile.rs and landing_tests.rs (only `build_slots: None` in Invocation literals), docs/records.md (one sentence). The Built note names each file and why (round-4 findings 1-6).
decisions.reason: `Invocation` has deny_unknown_fields and no Default (records.rs:681-706), so a new field needs a value at every literal and the compiler finds any missed one. The producer's spec and the record are built only in reading.rs and invocation.rs; no listed deliverable can set either. Nothing else in the deliverables carries the settings or reads the log. docs/records.md:93 lists the invocation's fields, so by the strangers default a reader of the record format should learn the new one. These six files are the minimum; the previous plans' admission.rs, run/planning.rs, tests/refusal_corpus.rs and tests/live.rs edits are dropped (decision 7).

rejected.why: verify.rs:366 and display.rs:1656 read them as command text; old records and readers would break.

risks.risk: The host's hook or Bash tool resolves PATH differently from the environment built here, so `cargo` runs the real cargo unslotted.
risks.mitigation: The hook denies a slotted cargo unless the first `cargo` on its own PATH is the wrapper and the variable is present (fails closed). If only the Bash tool differs, `slotted_seen` in the record exceeds the logged lines and `athena status` says so on the first real run. The Built note says hook/Bash equality was not measured.

risks.risk: If the hook process does not inherit the agent's env, every slotted producer cargo is denied.
risks.mitigation: The denial reason names the missing variable. fmt, metadata and tree stay allowed. Recorded as the Host question.

risks.risk: Starvation: the producer wait cap (540 s) is below build_age_promote_s (600 s), so a producer ticket never promotes into the check class, and a retry gets a fresh ticket with no age (slots.rs:245-251). With max_check_slots = 1, a steady stream of checks can starve producers to exit 75.
risks.mitigation: promote_s is left equal for every process (is_head agreement). The property is pinned by a slots.rs test and stated in the Built note and CHANGELOG. The User question asks for a governance change to build_age_promote_s. Producers get a clear exit 75 and may retry; checks hold slots briefly.

risks.risk: Wrapper install (reading.rs) and PATH env (env.rs) could diverge and deny every slotted cargo, or install an unused wrapper.
risks.mitigation: Both gate on `side == Side::Produce`; the reading.rs pair test checks the Side::Produce spec has the wrapper and variables and others do not; the policy keys on Role::Producer, and run/producer.rs:166 is the only Side::Produce caller.

risks.risk: A cargo started inside a slotted command takes a second slot and times out.
risks.mitigation: ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD makes nested wrappers pass through; the nested test with slots=1 fails without it. The policy denies `NAME=value` prefixes (policy.rs:546), so the agent cannot set the marker.

risks.risk: New tests inherit slot variables when a later producer runs them through its own wrapper.
risks.mitigation: All children go through `scrubbed()`; `real_cargo` takes explicit arguments; `slot_exec_tests_do_not_inherit_the_slot_variables` fails if the scrub is dropped.

risks.risk: If the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed, its child cargo keeps running without a slot.
risks.mitigation: Group kills (athena stop, deadlines) reach the whole tree because the child stays in the agent's group; test (d) checks it. The single-process-kill gap is stated in the Built note.

risks.risk: Counting held slots briefly try-locks free slot files and can make another waiting head miss a slot for one poll (250 ms).
risks.mitigation: The count runs only after a win; cost is at most one poll of extra wait; tests use `>=`/`<=` with forced barriers; the Built note mentions it.

risks.risk: The recorded peak is sampled only at producer-command starts, so it can undercount.
risks.mitigation: The status line labels it 'when a producer command started'; the Built note calls it a lower bound; the overlap test measures real concurrency.

risks.risk: Slots held for `cargo run` and `cargo test` last as long as the program runs and can block checks for up to the Bash timeout (athena.toml:65).
risks.mitigation: Stated as a known cost in the Built note; the wait cap bounds other waiters, who get 75 or a held check.

risks.risk: A producer retries in a loop after exit 75; timed-out waits are not in the record.
risks.mitigation: The message says to try again later; the Built note states that timed-out waits are not recorded.

risks.risk: The unslotted note can overcount: denied commands appear in commands_run, and compound commands are split heuristically.
risks.mitigation: The note says denied commands count; `slotted_cargo_commands` has unit tests for `&&`, `;`, `|` and `cargo fmt --check`; the note is skipped for the fake driver.

risks.risk: The timeout test needs a real wait of about one second because wait_s is in whole seconds.
risks.mitigation: wait_s = 1 and bounded 10 s poll loops; no sleeps order events.

risks.risk: Stale settings or log files from an earlier invocation of the same job (send-back passes).
risks.mitigation: `agent_spec` rewrites the settings and wrapper on each producer invocation; `invoke_and_record` removes a stale log before the run and the log after it; a test covers the stale log.

risks.risk: Invocation literals outside the deliverable list are missed.
risks.mitigation: The edits are listed by file and line; `cargo test --locked` and clippy fail on any missed literal.

risks.risk: Scope: six files outside the listed deliverables change (findings 1-6).
risks.mitigation: Each is the only place that can do its job or a compile-forced literal; the Built note names each and why; no step-3 file and no governance file changes.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/slot_exec.rs, names prefixed `slot_exec_`, run the real athena binary (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")) against a real SlotQueue over the same temp dir with limit 1 and probe with `SlotQueue::try_acquire`. Every child Command goes through `scrubbed()`. (a) `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- sh -c 'touch started; wait for release'`: after `started` appears try_acquire is None; after release and exit it is Some. (b) A symlink `bin/cargo` to the athena binary and a fake real `cargo` script written at run time into another temp dir, PATH=bin:real: `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy` and `check` each hold the slot while running and free it after; `cargo fmt --check` does not hold it. (c) A command that runs `kill -KILL $$`: wrapper exit 137 and the slot is free. (d) The wrapper in its own process group with `sh -c 'sleep 30 & sleep 30'`; the test calls `athena_agent::procs::kill_group(pgid, GRACE)`; the slot is free and `group_alive(pgid)` is false within a bounded 10 s poll. (e) Re-entrancy: slots=1, wait_s=5, `build-slot -- sh -c 'cargo build'` with PATH=bin:real exits 0 well before 5 s and the log has one line. (f) `slot_exec_tests_do_not_inherit_the_slot_variables`: variables set before `scrubbed()` are absent from `sh -c env`. Unit tests in slot_exec.rs call `real_cargo(path, self_path)` with explicit arguments.
demonstrations.observes: The slot is held exactly while the command runs and free afterwards; all four subcommands take a slot and fmt does not; a signal death and a group kill free the slot and end the whole tree; a nested cargo does not wait for a second slot; tests do not inherit slot variables.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the lock, try_acquire during the command returns Some and 'held' fails. Without release at exit or signal, the probe after returns None. Without the ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD guard, test (e) waits 5 s, exits 75 and fails. With isolate, (d) leaves the grandchild alive. Without `scrubbed()`, (f) finds the variables.

demonstrations.method: Test `slot_exec_second_producer_waits_for_the_first_then_runs`: settings slots=1. Wrapper A runs `sh -c 'touch a_started; wait for release; touch a_ended'`. After `a_started`, wrapper B (own log file) runs `sh -c 'test -e a_ended && touch b_ran_after_a'`. Poll (10 s deadline) until `SlotQueue::waiting() == 1`; assert `b_ran_after_a` is absent. Create `release`; wait for both. Assert `b_ran_after_a` exists, B exited 0, and B's log line has queued_s > 0 and slots_held == 1. A second test `slot_exec_peak_is_bounded_by_the_limit`: slots=2, three wrappers; A and B each wait for the other's start marker so they overlap, C queues behind. Commands append start/end marks to one shared file and the test computes the greatest overlap. Assert overlap == 2 (forced), C starts after one ended, largest slots_held in the logs is >= 2 and <= 2. A control runs two unwrapped commands the same way and must read overlap 2 with limit 1.
demonstrations.observes: B waits behind A, runs only after A's command ended, and its recorded queued_s is above zero; no more than the limit run at once.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the queue, B runs while A still holds the only slot, `a_ended` is absent, `b_ran_after_a` is never created and the test fails; the peak test's overlap reads 3. Without the recorded wait, queued_s is 0 and the greater-than-zero assertion fails.

open_questions: User: The request says the job is 'held, not failed' when no slot frees, but design section 4 (agent-and-build-slots.md:164-165) leaves the decision to the producer after exit 75. The plan builds the design's version (no run-level hold for producer commands) and says so in the Built note and CHANGELOG. Do you want a real hold for a producer whose command times out? That needs job-state access from the wrapper or a driver-level mapping, and edits to the out-of-scope step-3 files.

User: With the shipped config the producer's wait is capped at 540 s, below build_age_promote_s (600 s), so a producer ticket cannot age into the check class and a steady stream of checks can starve it to exit 75. Do you want a governance job to set build_age_promote_s below the cap (for example 300 s) or raise the Bash timeouts in athena.toml (not touched here)?

User: Should producer requests be ordered by the job's priority tier (urgent, then high, then the rest) as design section 4 describes? The plan leaves it out: the queue has one producer class ordered by time asked, and step 4 of section 8 does not name it.
User: Should the verifier's own cargo commands (verifier_commands, athena.toml:76) also be wrapped? The request says producer commands only; the plan leaves them out and says so in the Built note.

Host: Does the PreToolUse hook process run with the same PATH and environment as Claude Code's Bash tool, or does a shell profile snapshot put another cargo first? Nothing in the repository shows it. The hook's PATH rule and the status note on unslotted cargo commands are how a difference would appear.
